name: Gant
why: The New Haven shirtmaker that invented the locker loop and made Ivy’s button-downs; Swedish-owned since 1999, with no US store of its own today.
origin: Founded in 1949 in New Haven, Connecticut, USA by Bernard Gantmacher with sons Marty and Elliot Gant.

craft_evidence.owned: NONE today (evidence: supply-chain strategy PDF speaks only of "manufacturing partners"/"suppliers"); historical owned New Haven factories 130 Haven St (1955) and 40 Sargent Dr (1966) per Daily Nutmeg 2021 (evidence, historical only)
craft_evidence.mills: Abraham Moon (British Tweed Decker Jacket, "made in England by Abraham Moon mill") - evidence, 1 of 16 PDPs read; others name none (selvedge jeans: shuttle loom, no mill)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: "Since our beginnings in New Haven in 1949"; Bernard Gantmacher with sons Marty and Elliot founded Gant of New Haven (brand claim, corroborated by Daily Nutmeg 2021 and Wikipedia); Y
craft_evidence.process: construction features only (button-down collar, box pleat, locker loop; selvedge "woven on a vintage shuttle loom"; oz weights on denim) - no making process published
craft_evidence.reasoning: Gant owns no making today and names no makers; one PDP of 16 read names a mill (Abraham Moon tweed) and a few state fabric origin in prose ("Italian lambswool", "Italian cashmere"). Heritage is dated and placed (New Haven 1949) and independently corroborated, including former owned New Haven factories, but that is history, not current making. Composition and made-in sit in a collapsed accordion not reachable by fetch, so the score could rise if made-in or mills prove common there.

ownership.owner: MF Brands Group (Swiss, private; formerly Maus Frères International, renamed 2020) - the brands arm of Maus Frères SA; Maus Frères took Gant private 2008
